accepted.question_text: For the infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian with short-range or finite-range interaction considered in the paper, namely a system of the form H = sum_{j in Z^d} omega_j I_j + epsilon sum_{<i,j>} f_{i,j}(I_i, I_j; phi_i, phi_j), where the perturbation is short range or finite range and the frequencies are weakly correlated, KAM tori are constructed when the initial actions are strongly localized or even decay weaker than exponentially. Does there also exist an infinite-dimensional KAM torus when the initial actions decay only polynomially, in the sense that the action profile satisfies epsilon_j = I_j^0 approximately |j|^{-M} for some sufficiently large M > 0?

evidence.quote: In 1986, Frohlich, Spencer and Wayne[9] generalized Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) theorem to infinite dimensional Hamiltonian H = sum_{j in Z^d} omega_j I_j + epsilon sum_{<i,j>} f_{i,j}(I_i,I_j;phi_i,phi_j) with symplectic structure sum_j dI_j wedge dphi_j where f is of short range.

The initial conditions (1.17) implies that the action (or the amplitude) decays too fast such that the infinite dimensional KAM tori look like to be of finite dimension. Weaker restrictions were later suggested in Poschel[18]: epsilon_j = I_j^0 approximately exp(-(log|j|)^(1+alpha)) with some alpha > 0. Kuksin[15] and Bourgain[6] proposed the following open problem: Problem 1. Is there any infinite dimensional KAM tori for the initial conditions with polynomial decay epsilon_j = I_j^0 approximately |j|^{-M} with some large M > 0?

accepted.question_text: Consider a Hamiltonian system whose linearized operator, for example -Delta_f + v, has pure point spectrum, with part of that pure point spectrum dense in some finite interval. If the nonlinear part of the Hamiltonian is not short range, as in Hamiltonian partial differential equations posed on the whole space, do KAM tori still exist for that system?
accepted.context_brief: Pure point spectrum with non-short-range nonlinearity

evidence.quote: Here is no any conditions imposed on the normal frequencies lambda_n's, except that which are of pure point spectra and are non-zero. Therefore, these frequencies can densely distributed on an finite interval. For example, they can be all rational number in the interval [1,2].

Problem 2. Assume that the linearized operator (-Delta_f +v, for example,) of a hamiltonian system is of pure point spectra, part of which is dense in some finite interval, and assume that the nonlinear part of the Hamiltonian is not of short rang (in partial differential equations defined in the whole space, for example). Are there any KAM tori for the system? This problem is apparently open.

accepted.question_text: Consider a Hamiltonian system whose linearized operator, for example -Delta_f + v, has continuous spectrum containing an interval. Can such a system admit any KAM tori, even in the case where the Hamiltonian itself may still have short-range interactions?

evidence.quote: Remark 3. We have seen that the pure point spectra property is of key importance for the existence of quasi-periodic breathers for Hamiltonian with short range. If W(x) = 1/2 x^2 + ..., the linearized system of (2.6) is of continuous spectra which is the whole of the interval [beta,beta +1].

Problem 3. Assume that the linearized operator (-Delta_f + v, for example,) of a hamiltonian system contains continuous spectra which consist of an interval. Are there any KAM tori for the system? even if the system may be of short range. In general, the answer trends to be no.
